Component header.description: The file headers. @tag is worth setting: the default is the type name lower-cased and cannot produce a hyphen, so a compound name silently answers to something no stylesheet matches.

body: /// ⚠ Signal-backed, and it has to be. BuildContext.Child<T> constructs a
///     component, mounts it — which runs <c>Build</c> — and assigns its parameters
/// afterwards. So every effect this component made has already read the property
///     once, with whatever the default was, and a plain property assigned later notifies nobody.
Signal-backed parameter.description: A component parameter that actually updates. A plain property assigned after the mount reaches no effect.

Keyed loop.description: ⚠ Key on the item's value when the item is immutable data, and on the object only when that object holds signals: a surviving key keeps its region and its body is NOT re-run, so per-item bindings go on reading the value the key first appeared with.

Conditional.description: ⚠ `@if (x is { } y)` does not work: the condition becomes an effect and the body a separate build, so a pattern variable declared in the test is not in scope inside the branch. The fix is a property, not a pattern.

Element reference.description: Hands the element back to a member, assigned in the straight-line body and certainly by OnComposed. ⚠ Refused inside a @for — use refs, which is keyed.

Two-way binding.description: Two-way over a [UiProperty]. ⚠ The expression must be an assignable lvalue of the property's exact type — a Signal<T> needs its .Value, and the T has to match (string? not string, double not float for NumericInput.Number).

Value change.description: One-way out. Not an event: `on:` maps through a table of routed gestures and no entry in it can hand a handler a value.

Composed hook.description: Runs once the whole body has run, which is the first moment every ref is assigned. Re-run by a hot reload, because the body contains the assignments.
